title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 134
paragraphs: So much of the story is told by all the Greeks; but what followed the Parians alone report, and they say it happened like this. Miltiades, they say, was at a loss, when a woman came to speak with him, a Parian by birth named Timo who had been taken prisoner; she was an under-priestess of the chthonic goddesses. Coming into Miltiades's presence, she advised him that if it was of great importance to him to take Paros, he should do what she was about to suggest, and then she told him her meaning. So he crossed over to the hill that lies in front of the city and leapt over the fence of the temple of Demeter the Lawgiver, since he could not open the door; and having got over the fence, he went on towards the inner sanctuary, intending to do something inside — whether to lay hands on something that should not be touched, or whatever else he had in mind. When he reached the door, a sudden shuddering dread came over him and he set off to go back the way he had come; and as he leapt down from the wall of rough stones, his thigh was dislocated, or, as others say, he struck his knee against the wall.
